items.q: What capped Nate's income before the four upgrades?
items.a: Not raw intelligence — **output quality** and **production speed**. By default Claude is tuned to make you feel **productive**, not to make you **money**. He claims these upgrades **3×'d income in 30 days**.

items.q: How bad is AI sycophancy in measured studies?
items.a: The "Elephant" study: models fail to push back on framing ~**88%** of the time (humans ~**60%**). Personalization/memory makes agreement mode worse.

items.q: What does the `/roast` skill actually do?
items.a: Spins a **council of sub-agents** (contrarian, expansionist, first-principles, deep researcher, buyer, judge) that stress-test ideas before building. Verdicts: **green light, reshape, or kill** — plus the cheapest **48-hour validation** test.

items.q: What happened when the council roasted the $9 LinkedIn tool?
items.a: Scores of **2–8/10** and a reshape: kill the commodity **$9 wrapper**, keep the engine, target a narrow niche with **voice matching + scheduled posting** (later rebranded "Cadence").

~**40%** of Copilot-generated code had vulnerabilities (NYU). Nate's outreach agent claimed **100%** email delivery but only sent **25%**. Fix: verify before handoff, then **adversarial stress-test** after.

items.q: What did the live landing-page verification look like?
items.a: **Playwright CLI** screenshots at desktop + mobile until zero visible errors, then **22 form-submission** stress tests (valid + malformed) in a headed browser. First shot ~**65%**; verification gets ~**90%**.

items.q: When does context rot actually start?
items.a: **Well before the window fills** — longer conversations make Claude dumber even on simple tasks across **18 tested models**. More context is not better.

Nate finds `/compact` slow. Custom handoff captures **locked decisions, shipped files, running state, open questions, and "pick up here"**, then `/clear` + paste. Stay under ~**250K tokens**; use `/context` to audit token eaters.

items.q: How much do parallel sub-agents help?
items.a: Anthropic's parallel sub-agent team beat a single agent by **>90%** on internal evals. Each agent gets a **clean context window**; synthesize after. Final demo: **6 parallel agents** built a full GTM kit in ~**8 minutes**.

items.q: What problem does `/goal` solve at completion time?
items.a: Sets an **objective done condition**; a **separate evaluator model** grades each turn so the worker **can't declare itself done** — sycophancy control at the finish line. Your role shifts from builder to **reviewer/judge**.
